definition: A protocol extension that encrypts the Server Name Indication (SNI) field in TLS connections, preventing network observers from seeing which specific website you're visiting.
metaDescription: Learn about Encrypted SNI (ESNI), a privacy technology that hides which websites you visit from network observers and internet service providers.
simpleExplanation: When you visit a website, your browser normally sends the website's name in plain text, even over secure connections. Encrypted SNI hides this information by encrypting the website name, making it harder for others to track your browsing.
whyItMatters: Without Encrypted SNI, your ISP, network administrators, and other intermediaries can see exactly which websites you visit, even when using HTTPS. This creates privacy risks and enables censorship and surveillance of your online activities.
technicalDetail: Encrypted SNI encrypts the Server Name Indication field using a public key published in DNS records. This prevents passive network monitoring from identifying the target server while still allowing proper TLS handshakes. It's been succeeded by Encrypted Client Hello (ECH) which provides broader protection.

examples.explanation: Without Encrypted SNI, the coffee shop's network can see you're visiting specific news sites or social media platforms. With it enabled, they only see encrypted traffic to a general server.
Your internet provider normally sees every website domain you visit for advertising or data collection. Encrypted SNI prevents this domain-level tracking while maintaining secure connections.
Companies can block specific websites by monitoring SNI data. Encrypted SNI makes such granular filtering more difficult, though organizations can still block entire IP addresses.
